findings.title: KeyError if integration.metadata lacks 'sender'
findings.body: The check `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` assumes that `sender` is always present in the integration metadata. However, `build_integration` only adds `sender` to metadata when `state.get("sender")` is truthy (line ~377). If the GitHub webhook did not include a sender (or did not run before this view), `integration.metadata["sender"]` raises KeyError, surfacing as a 500 instead of the intended graceful `error(...)` response. The code should use `integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login")` (or guard the lookup explicitly) so that a missing sender is treated like any other invalid installation request.

findings.title: safe_urlopen not wrapped in try/except
findings.body: The line `req = safe_urlopen(url=ghip.get_oauth_access_token_url(), data=data)` performs the OAuth code-for-token exchange, but unlike the subsequent `safe_urlread`/`parse_qsl` block, it is not wrapped in a try/except. Any network failure, DNS error, TLS error, or non-2xx HTTP response will raise an uncaught exception and turn into a 500, instead of returning the generic `error(...)` page that the surrounding code clearly intends to surface for failed exchanges. This contradicts the PR's stated guarantee that 'If GitHub could not generate correct access_token from the code' the user is shown the error dialog.

findings.title: No test for OAuth state mismatch
findings.body: The PR description explicitly promises that the pipeline fails 'If there is a mismatch between state parameter supplied by user and pipeline signature', and the code at line 412 implements that check (`if request.GET.get("state") != pipeline.signature: return error(...)`). However, no test in `tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py` exercises this path by supplying a callback with a wrong `state`. Without such a test, regressions to the state check (or to how the signature is generated/compared) would go unnoticed.

findings.title: No test for failed OAuth code exchange (wrong/reused code)
findings.body: The PR description promises failure 'If GitHub could not generate correct access_token from the code (wrong or attempt of re-use of code)'. The branch at line 431 handles this, but no test in `test_integration.py` stubs `https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token` to return a body without `access_token` (or to return an error response) and asserts that the integration-failed template is shown. Coverage of the happy OAuth path exists, but the negative path the PR advertises is untested.

findings.title: No test for get_user_info missing 'login'
findings.body: The branch `if "login" not in authenticated_user_info: return error(...)` (line 435) is not covered by any test. There is no scenario in `test_integration.py` where the stub for `https://api.github.com/user` returns a payload without `login`, so a regression that, for example, accidentally trusts a different field or fails to validate the response would not be caught.

findings.title: No test for missing 'sender' in integration metadata
findings.body: The user-mismatch check at line 503 reads `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]`. There is no test that creates an Integration record whose metadata lacks `sender` (e.g., by emulating an installation webhook that omits the sender, or by manually constructing metadata). Combined with the fact that `build_integration` only sets `sender` when `state.get("sender")` is truthy, this means the new KeyError-on-missing-sender path is completely untested.

findings.title: test_installation_not_found may not exercise the intended code path
findings.body: The test stubs `/app/installations/{installation_id}` with a 404 and uses a hardcoded state `ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05` for the OAuth callback. After the first GET (which binds `installation_id` to pipeline state), the actual pipeline signature is whatever Sentry's Pipeline produces for that state; it almost certainly does not equal `ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05`. The test then asserts only the generic `b"Invalid installation request."` string, which is also produced by the state-mismatch branch. As a result the test passes whether the state check rejects the request or the not-found branch fires, and the 404 stub for `/app/installations/...` is never actually consumed (that endpoint is only called in `build_integration`, which never runs because the pipeline errors out first). The test should drive the OAuth callback with the real pipeline signature (or use a different setup) so it deterministically exercises the not-found branch.

findings.title: test_github_user_mismatch ignores init_path_1 response
findings.body: In `test_github_user_mismatch`, `self.client.get(init_path_1)` is called but its response is neither asserted nor stored. If that request fails (e.g., 500, redirect to error template), the test silently continues and the subsequent webhook/install assertions lose their meaning because the pipeline state from the first request was never established. The response should be asserted (status 302 to the OAuth authorize URL) so a regression in the initial pipeline bootstrap is caught.

findings.title: Generic error masks real cause from logs
findings.body: Several distinct failure modes (state mismatch, missing access_token, missing user login, sender mismatch, missing integration) all funnel into the same `error(...)` response with the user-facing message 'Invalid installation request.' and no logging of the specific reason. Because `error()` is reached from multiple call sites without any distinguishing log line, an operator triaging production failures has no way to tell from logs or user reports which branch was hit. At minimum, each `return error(...)` site should emit a `logger.info`/`warning` with the specific cause (e.g., 'oauth state mismatch', 'oauth token exchange failed', 'github user mismatch').
